newsitem.title: USA: First Lady takes up capital city's cause.
newsitem.headline: First Lady takes up capital city's cause.

text.p: First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton took up the U.S. capital's cause Thursday, speaking out on behalf of the financially troubled city and pledging that the White House would help tackle its problems.

"Much has been written and debated about what is wrong with Washington and what isn't working and all of us will do our part to meet those challenges," Clinton said at a press conference unveiling a new federal investment program for the city and other impoverished areas.
"But let's not forget everything that is right about Washington and the people who live and work here," she said to loud applause from local officials and businessmen.

After backing her husband's failed effort to reform the health care system, Clinton has taken a low profile on public policy matters for several years. But she has signaled plans to take a visible role in rehabilitating Washington D.C.
Aides said Clinton would address the issue again Friday in announcing she will donate some of the proceeds of her book, "It takes a Village," to a local children's hospital.
The first lady Thursday launched a $20 million federal pilot program to create tiny, community-owned banks in Washington, Baltimore, Maryland and a rural section of Mississippi.
